All data gathered. Final answer below.

## Collection scope (validate.sh:296 invocation; ignores = load, benchmarks, e2e, chaos)

**Dirs collected: 6 + 1 top-level file. Collected test files: 895**

| Dir | test_*.py | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `backend/tests/unit/` | 675 | plain collection |
| `backend/tests/integration/` | 209 | 173 at top level, 15 `services/`, 7 `repositories/`, 6 `api/`, 4 `api/routes/`, 1 each in `websocket/ models/ database/ core/` |
| `backend/tests/contracts/` | 4 | `test_api_contracts.py`, `test_openapi_schema_validation.py`, `test_schemathesis_contracts.py`, `test_websocket_contracts.py` |
| `backend/tests/security/` | 5 | `test_admin_access_control.py`, `test_api_security.py`, `test_auth_security.py`, `test_docker_compose_security.py`, `test_input_validation.py` |
| `backend/tests/gpu/` | 1 | `test_detector_integration.py` — collected but all tests `@pytest.mark.gpu`, deselected by addopts `-m 'not gpu'` |
| `backend/tests/fixtures/` | 0 | data only (images, synthetic) |
| `backend/tests/utils/` | 0 | helper modules only (`async_helpers.py`, `assertions.py`, `strategies.py`, `replay_helpers.py`) |
| `backend/tests/test_utils.py` | 1 (top-level) | collected, contains **0 test functions** |

Also collected-but-empty: `integration/test_helpers.py` (0 test funcs). Non-test top-level files (`factories.py`, `matchers.py`, `strategies.py`, `conftest.py`, etc.) are imported as helpers, not collected. No `test_*.py` exists outside `backend/tests/` under `backend/`.

## (1) Integration files: 209 total, marks, session fixtures

- **109/209 carry explicit `pytest.mark.integration`**; the other **100** (19 have zero pytest markers at all, including 2 helper-only files) are **auto-marked** by root `backend/tests/conftest.py` `pytest_collection_modifyitems` (:372-447): any item whose fspath contains `/integration/` gets `integration` + a 5s timeout applied automatically. So all 209 effectively carry the mark.
- **Container-needing session fixtures live in `integration/conftest.py`, not test files**: `postgres_container` (:328 session), `redis_container` (:367 session) — they start testcontainers **only if** local PG (5432) / Redis (6379) are unreachable (dev fallback to local services). No zero test files define their own session-scoped fixtures. Usage: 60 integration files request `integration_db`; 25 request `real_redis`.
- `repositories/` tests additionally get auto `xdist_group("repository_tests_serial")` + `serial` markers (shared-DB, conftest warns if xdist enabled when targeted directly; under the full run they are just serialized).

## (2) Security / contracts dirs (CI treats separately)

- `backend/tests/contracts/` — 4 files, `ci.yml:964` runs them as a dedicated job.
- `backend/tests/security/` — 5 files, `ci.yml:2336` (`test_admin_access_control.py` also solo at ci.yml:2352).
- Neither dir has any `pytest.mark.*` usage (no `security`/`contract` markers are even registered in `pyproject.toml:477`, and `--strict-markers` would fail unregistered ones). Both have their own conftest (mock-based, no containers). Under validate.sh they are collected together with unit+integration in the same combined run.

## (3) Non-integration files importing testcontainers / starting containers

- **Zero.** `grep testcontainers` across `backend/tests` hits only: `backend/tests/test_utils.py` (TYPE_CHECKING-only import of `PostgresContainer`/`RedisContainer`, no runtime import, no container start), `integration/conftest.py` (all `testcontainers` imports inside fixture bodies or `TYPE_CHECKING`), and docstrings/AGENTS.md. `unit/`, `contracts/`, `security/`, `gpu/`: no testcontainers references at all.
- No container is started at **module-import time** anywhere. Container starts are fixture-scoped:
  - `integration/conftest.py:351` `PostgresContainer` / `:390` `RedisContainer("redis:7-alpine")` — session-scoped, lazily instantiated when first requested.
  - `integration/test_mqtt_integration.py:52-63` — **module-scoped** fixture starting `eclipse-mosquitto:2.0` via `DockerContainer`, guarded by `pytest.importorskip("testcontainers")`.
  - `integration/test_alembic_migrations.py:33-38` — class-scoped `PostgresContainer("postgres:16")`, but the whole class is `@pytest.mark.skip` (:23) so it never starts.
  - `integration/test_orchestrator_integration.py` — mentions `DockerContainer` but it's the `docker.models.containers` type (TYPE_CHECKING) for the app's own orchestrator service, not testcontainers.

## (4) `backend/tests/integration/conftest.py` module-scope heaviness

**No cv2 / torch / sentence_transformers at module scope.** Module-scope imports (:30-43): `asyncio, logging, os, tempfile, collections, pathlib, unittest.mock, pytest, xdist, sqlalchemy.inspect` + `backend.tests.test_utils` helpers. All `testcontainers` and `psycopg2` imports are lazy (inside fixture bodies) or TYPE_CHECKING-guarded. **Collection is not slowed by ML libs from this conftest.**

Caveats affecting the whole combined run:
- Root `backend/tests/conftest.py` (2507 lines) imports `psycopg2` and `hypothesis` at module scope — paid once by all tests.
- **`integration/services/test_stgcn_loader.py:6-7` has top-level `import torch`** (no `importorskip` guard). This is the single heavy collection-time import in the tree; torch 2.9.1+cpu is installed in the env so it succeeds, costing ~1-2s once during collection, not per-test.
- No other file top-level-imports `torch`/`cv2`/`sentence_transformers`/`ultralytics` (grep-verified across unit/integration/contracts/security/gpu).
- 4 tracked zero-byte test files will be collected as empty modules: `integration/test_zone_baselines.py`, `unit/test_matchers.py`, `unit/core/test_result.py`, `unit/api/routes/test_cameras_heatmap.py` (already allowlisted per commit a4c061fd).

Key files: `/agents/agent-nemo2/workspace/scripts/validate.sh:296`, `/agents/agent-nemo2/workspace/backend/tests/conftest.py:372-447`, `/agents/agent-nemo2/workspace/backend/tests/integration/conftest.py:328-400`, `/agents/agent-nemo2/workspace/backend/tests/test_utils.py:24-25`, `/agents/agent-nemo2/workspace/backend/tests/integration/services/test_stgcn_loader.py:7`, `/agents/agent-nemo2/workspace/pyproject.toml:470-477`.

## 1. Exact timeout values integration tests get

Enforcement lives in `/agents/agent-nemo2/workspace/backend/tests/conftest.py` (not the integration conftest). Neither conftest has `addinivalue_line` entries for timeout — the only `addinivalue_line` calls there are for `flaky` and `chaos` markers (backend/tests/conftest.py:300-307). The `markers = [...]` docs in pyproject.toml:477-483 that say "5s timeout" / "30s" are descriptive strings only; actual values are applied by `_apply_timeout_marker()` (backend/tests/conftest.py:346-369), called from `pytest_collection_modifyitems` (line 445-447):

- Priority 1: CLI `--timeout=0` disables all timeouts (backend/tests/conftest.py:397-400)
- Priority 2: explicit `@pytest.mark.timeout(N)` anywhere on the item (incl. module-level `pytestmark`) — unchanged
- Priority 3: `slow` marker → `timeout(30)`
- Priority 4: `"/integration/" in fspath` → `timeout(5)`
- Fallback: ini `timeout = 5` (pyproject.toml:471)

So: **integration tests get 5s unless overridden; slow-marked integration tests get 30s.** Per-file/override markers found (all keep `func_only=true` from ini since the marker doesn't set it — pytest_timeout.py:405-406 falls back to `config._env_timeout_func_only`):

- `backend/tests/integration/test_dlq_retry_handler_integration.py:49` — module `pytestmark = pytest.mark.timeout(60)`
- `backend/tests/integration/test_transaction_rollback.py:200,450,542,612,776` — 15/10/15/10/10
- `backend/tests/integration/test_health_checks.py:296` — timeout(15) on `test_health_check_timeout_handling`
- `backend/tests/integration/test_cache_service_integration.py:225,263` — 15/10
- `backend/tests/integration/services/test_cache_behavior.py:149` — 10

Note: the pyproject docs claiming "e2e/gpu: 60s timeout" are not enforced anywhere — no conftest applies `timeout(60)` for those directories; only explicit in-file markers do (backend/tests/e2e/test_pipeline_integration.py:318, test_gpu_pipeline.py:396,504,558).

## 2. asyncio.sleep > 2s in backend/tests/integration (call phase)

| file:line | duration |
|---|---|
| `backend/tests/integration/test_health_checks.py:316` | 7 |
| `backend/tests/integration/test_file_watcher_filesystem.py:598` | 3.0 |
| `backend/tests/integration/test_cache_service_integration.py:282` | 2.5 |

Correction to the premise: **`test_api_protection.py` has `asyncio.sleep(1.5)` ten times, not twice** (lines 262, 349, 421, 469, 528, 578, 628, 672, 736, 795 — working tree matches HEAD, commit 294d1a7f "F3 repair"). At exactly 2.0: `test_file_watcher_filesystem.py:646`, `test_file_watcher_integration.py:551`, `test_cache_db_consistency.py:393`, `test_shutdown_sequence.py:473`, `test_mqtt_integration.py:72` (that one is inside a **module-scoped fixture**, i.e. setup — exempt under func_only). The six `asyncio.sleep(10)` calls (test_worker_supervisor.py:105,147,217,279,360,387; test_shutdown_sequence.py:258) are cancelled immediately and don't consume wall time.

## 3. Retry loops / long wait_for

- `backend/tests/integration/test_redis_pubsub.py:451,507` — `wait_for(listener_task, timeout=10.0)` **inside the test call phase**; the TimeoutError is caught, but the 10s burn happens before pytest-timeout's 5s would. Highest wait_for value in call phase.
- Fixture-teardown wait_for (exempt under func_only): integration conftest.py:969 (10s `_cleanup_test_cameras`), 975 (5s `close_db`), 1070 (10s `truncate_all`), 1242 (5s `client.disconnect`), 1463 (10s `_cleanup_test_data`), 1528/1779 (5s redis delete).
- Retry loops: `test_transaction_rollback.py:735` (3 attempts, DB only, no sleeps), `test_memory_stability.py:349` (range(3)), `test_dlq_retry_handler_integration.py` (module timeout(60)), `test_health_monitor_integration.py:541,892` (sleep(1.0)/0.8 retry-cycle waits).

## 4. What timeout_func_only=true excludes (pytest_timeout.py source)

`/agents/agent-nemo2/workspace/.venv/lib/python3.14/site-packages/pytest_timeout.py`:

- `pytest_runtest_protocol` hookwrapper (lines ~181-193): arms the timer **only if `settings.func_only is False`** — so with func_only=true this hook never arms.
- `pytest_runtest_call` hookwrapper (lines 202-216): arms the timer **only if `func_only is True`**, wrapping just the call phase.

Confirmed: **with func_only=true, fixture setup and teardown are fully exempt** — testcontainers startup, `integration_db`/`client`/`clean_tables` fixture time, and all conftest teardown waits cannot trip the per-test timeout. Timer runs via `threading.Timer`; on expiry `timeout_timer` (line 505) dumps stacks and calls **`os._exit(1)`** (line 542) — killing the entire xdist worker, not just the failing test. No `session_timeout` is set in pyproject, so there is no session-level backstop.

## 5. Verdict — top risks with warm testcontainers (setup cost excluded)

1. **`test_redis_pubsub.py:451,507`** — `wait_for(..., timeout=10.0)` inside call phase vs 5s budget. Any pub/sub lag on arm64 → 5s timer fires first → worker `os._exit(1)`. Highest structural risk.
2. **`test_file_watcher_filesystem.py`** — 5s budget with synchronous PIL image synthesis on arm64 (CPU-bound, blocks the loop): `test_rapid_file_creation_no_events_lost` (20 × `create_test_image` + 3.0s sleep, line 598), `test_concurrent_creation_across_cameras` (2.0s sleep, line 646), `test_processes_large_image_file` (1.5s, line 500), `test_polling_mode_detects_files` (1.5s, line 1050). Compute + sleep can easily exceed 5s.
3. **`test_api_protection.py`** — 10 tests × sleep(1.5) + 2-4 Argon2id hash/verify ops per test (`PasswordHasher(time_cost=3, memory_cost=65536, parallelism=4)`, backend/services/auth_service.py:25-29 — expensive on arm64, runs synchronously inside request handlers) + several middleware-stack HTTP round-trips, all inside a 5s call budget. Heaviest: `test_setup_flow_enables_endpoints`, `test_api_key_auth_works`, `test_admin_can_create_additional_users`, `test_session_cookie_auth_works_via_me`.
4. **`test_health_checks.py::test_health_check_timeout_handling`** — 7s sleep (line 316) is the single largest in-call sleep. It survives only because of its explicit `timeout(15)`; if that marker is ever dropped it dies instantly. Its own assertion (`elapsed < 12.0`) also eats 5 of the 15s.
5. **`test_cache_db_consistency.py:393`** — sleep(2.0) + camera insert + cache reload, 5s budget: tight on slow arm64.
6. **`test_mqtt_integration.py`** — the 2s broker-startup sleep is exempt (module-scoped fixture), but the call phase does real paho connect/publish against a real mosquitto on arm64: moderate risk of 5s blowout.
7. **`test_health_monitor_integration.py:541`** — 1.0s wait for retry cycles + backoff math: moderate.

Effectively safe: `test_cache_service_integration.py:282` (2.5s sleep but explicit timeout(10)), all `test_transaction_rollback.py` classes (10-15s overrides), `test_dlq_retry_handler_integration.py` (60s), `slow`-marked tests (30s, e.g. `test_orphan_cleanup_service.py`), and `test_shutdown_sequence.py:473` (2.0s sleep capped by `wait_for(..., 1.0)` → ~1s wall).
